title: Leanor: A Learning-Based Accelerator for Efficient Approximate Nearest Neighbor Search via Reduced Memory Access
problem: Approximate Nearest Neighbor Search (ANNS) is computationally and memory-intensive. IVFPQ implementations have high precision but suffer from redundant memory accesses due to traversing non-nearest neighbor vectors, and existing learned indexes fail to handle high-dimensional data efficiently.
motivation: ANNS is fundamental to recommendation systems, vector databases, and similarity search applications, but memory bandwidth waste on irrelevant vectors significantly limits performance.
method: Leanor employs learned indexes to optimize ANNS by learning data distribution patterns. The accelerator architecture predicts and skips traversal of non-nearest neighbor vectors in IVFPQ, reducing memory access overhead while maintaining search accuracy for high-dimensional data.
key_novelty: Learning-based accelerator that extends learned indexes to high-dimensional ANNS by intelligently reducing redundant memory accesses in IVFPQ through data-distribution-aware traversal optimization.
contributions: Leanor accelerator architecture for learned-optimized ANNS
Memory access reduction technique for IVFPQ through learned traversal patterns
First learned index system for high-dimensional vector search
Efficiency improvements over traditional IVFPQ implementation
limitations: Not discussed in the abstract provided.
primary_theme: Learning-based hardware acceleration for high-dimensional nearest neighbor search
